newsitem.title: USA: Sun Micro sees continuing Java momentum.
newsitem.headline: Sun Micro sees continuing Java momentum.

text.p: Sun Microsystems Inc Chairman and Chief Executive Scott McNealy said he sees continued momentum for Sun's Java technologies, with a wide-ranging product rollout due at the end of October.
"The Java momentum continues unabated...," McNealy said in a teleconference call with analysts, adding that this was happening without major advertising or promotional spending.
Michael Lehman, Sun Microsystems's chief financial officer, told analysts the company's first fiscal quarter gross margin of 47.7 percent was the "highest level in many years."

Lehman said the company had increased its expected levels of employment for JavaSoft, the unit spearheading the development of the new Java technologies. Java is central to the company's strategy of developing network-centered systems, such as the Internet and private corporate networks known as Intranets.
"With the increased focus on Java, we also will be attempting to ramp up the head count to as many as 500 employees in JavaSoft by the end of FY97," he said.
"That's up from the 300 to 350 or so that we've been targeting for our last couple of quarters," he told analysts.
Lehman also noted that the company had completed an "opportunistic buyback program" in the September quarter. The program was approved by the board in July of 1995.
"We repurchased nearly 4.4 million shares at a cost of approximately $236 million on that program during Q1," he said.

The company had announced a new systematic stock buyback program during the quarter in which it will purchase about $450 million during the next three years. The purchases will help reduce dilution related to issuance of stock through its 1990 Long-Term Equity Incentive Plan.
"We made minimal purchases during Q1 but have commenced activity under that program," he said, noting another plan has been in place to offset employee stock purchase plan dilution.

"So in total, we purchased approximately $270 million of stock under all programs during Q1, and over the past five years Sun has repurchased a total of approximately 64 million shares for around $1.3 billion," he said.
